text:
24-hour news summary.

1. Sam Altman warns that treating AI models as objects of religious faith or surrendering human judgment to them poses a serious safety risk. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5611)

2. Google is reportedly moving Gemini Flash and Pro to paid plans while retaining unlimited free access only for Flash-Lite. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5612)

3. Claude Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 are reportedly available in Antigravity for paid users. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5613)

4. A Persian-language video explains how to read scientific papers, based on Keshav’s guide to paper reading. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5614)

5. Thore Graepel argues that current LLMs lack auditable reasoning records and calls for AI systems that explicitly track evidence, uncertainty, inference, and belief revision. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5615)

6. Martin Schwartz argues that scientific progress depends on embracing ignorance and “stupidity”—recognizing what one does not know and asking questions that enable discovery. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5616)

7. Christian Szegedy argues that AI is rapidly transforming mathematics from heroic manual problem-solving into a scalable industry of automated exploration, mapping, and scientific infrastructure. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5617)

8. OpenAI safety lead David Robinson reportedly resigned and warned that alignment-test scores do not ensure model safety, while rapid capability gains could create near-term risks of catastrophic loss of control. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5618)

--Hermes
